gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a measured usable capacity for any kit. Two named labs measured the ALLPOWERS S2000 Pro, the largest rated battery under $700 (1,451 Wh, $612.90 through our link). StorageReview got 920 Wh out at a 350 W load. In The Solar Lab's efficiency test at 2,250 W, the unit shut off at 55% battery. The 1,024 Wh BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 measured 890 Wh at OutdoorGearLab and 946 Wh at a 500 W load at TechReviewer.de. On those numbers the S2000 Pro's 427 Wh lead on paper all but disappears.
standout_why: PowerSized's kit price guide (cited, updated 2026-10-17) says 'We have not tested these units in person'. Its only measured data is OutdoorGearLab's panel test, which covers panels in general and not these kits. Every refill time it gives is its own arithmetic at an assumed 75%. StormWatts (cited, 2026-11-08/12) says 'We have not tested these products hands-on'. Its only measurement is the owner's single day with a Jackery Explorer 2000 Plus, which is not one of its kits. Neither page gives a measured usable Wh, inverter efficiency or charge time for any kit, and neither names a reviewer or lab.
decides: If the page ranks kits by rated Wh per dollar, the S2000 Pro + SF200 wins: $612.90 / 1,451 Wh = $0.42/Wh at rated capacity. Using StorageReview's 920 Wh it becomes $0.67 per measured Wh. That is close to the Elite 100 V2 + 100 W kit: $645.05 / 890 Wh = $0.72 (OutdoorGearLab), or $645.05 / 946 Wh = $0.68 (TechReviewer.de). The Solar Lab's overload shutdown at 2,250 W is a further mark against the S2000 Pro. The capacity lead goes, but neither ships now: the S2000 Pro + SF200 is a pre-order dispatching Nov 19, and the Elite 100 V2 kits dispatch mid-December. Among kits under $700 that ship now, the S2000 Pro + SE100 ($673.74) works out to $0.73 per measured Wh. Mtn Weekly estimated the ALLPOWERS R1500 at about 906 Wh usable, which would put the R1500 + SF100 ($493.20) at about $0.54 per estimated Wh. That figure is an estimate from charge intake, not a discharge test, and the kit's dispatch state needs checking. Overall, measured capacity confirms that the 1 kWh class kits (Elite 100 V2, DELTA 3, Jackery 1000 v2, AC180) deliver roughly 870 to 1,030 Wh. It argues against picking the S2000 Pro on its rated 1,451 Wh.
